caption: Mule deer buck, front view, North Dakota badlands. Huge ears held out to the side, white throat patch, antlers that fork and fork again.
author: Matt Reinbold from USA
cardBack: Mule deer buck. Big mule ears, white throat patch, antlers that branch in forks (each beam splits, then splits again).

caption: Mule deer buck in sagebrush, Craters of the Moon, Idaho. Note the white rump and the thin white tail with a black tip.
author: NPS Photo

caption: Mule deer doe in snowy sagebrush, Wyoming. Grey winter coat, white rump, small tail held down.
author: USFWS Mountain-Prairie

caption: Mule deer doe, front view. No antlers, huge ears, pale face with a dark forehead.
author: USFWS Mountain-Prairie

caption: Three mule deer near Radium, British Columbia. Open pine and grass, typical Kootenay winter range.
author: Sir-Mister-Horse

caption: White tailed buck running in snow with the tail up. The tail is the flag: broad, flipped up, white underneath.
author: ForestWander

caption: White tailed doe trotting with the tail raised: the white flag of alarm.
author: HARRY W. McCORMACK ( TEABERRYEAGLE )

caption: White tailed doe, side view, in snow. Brown back, long brown tail, smaller ears than a mule deer.
author: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service - Midwest Region
cardBack: White tailed doe. No antlers, smaller ears than a mule deer, long wide brown tail with white edges.

caption: Mule deer buck in brush, Malheur refuge, Oregon. In cover, look for the ears and the antler tines first.
author: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service Headquarters

caption: Mule deer doe and two fawns from behind. Big white rump patches, thin rope tails with black tips.
author: USFWS Mountain-Prairie

caption: Mule deer doe and fawn half hidden in brush. In cover you often see only ears and a face.
author: USFWS Mountain-Prairie

caption: Mule deer at distance in sagebrush, eastern Oregon. Grey bodies, white rumps and big ears are what you pick out first.
author: BLM Oregon & Washington

caption: Mule deer fawn bedded and hiding in grass. Its mother is close by. Leave it alone.
author: USFWS Mountain Prairie

caption: Mule deer fawn in summer, North Dakota. White spots on a red brown coat; the spots fade by fall.
author: James St. John

caption: White tailed deer buck, side view, New Jersey. Brown tail with white edges, antler tines rising from one main beam.
author: Famartin
cardBack: White tailed buck. Smaller ears, wide brown tail with white edges, tines that grow up off one main beam.

caption: White tailed deer buck, front view. White band across the nose, white throat patch, tines off a main beam that sweeps forward.
author: Famartin

caption: White tailed deer bounding away on open prairie, Montana. Running long and low, tails up, not the stiff legged bounce of a mule deer.
author: NPS

caption: Bull moose, side view, in fall. Tall front shoulders, hump, long legs, broad flat antler palms.
author: Jacob W. Frank
cardBack: Bull moose. Black brown, horse sized, shoulder hump, long face, wide palmated (flat, hand shaped) antlers.

caption: Bull moose, front view, Grand Teton. Antlers spread wide like two open hands; heavy bulbous nose.
author: GrandTetonNPS

caption: Young bull moose with small spike and fork antlers, Grand Teton. Measure carefully: young bulls are often not legal.
author: GrandTetonNPS

caption: Cow moose feeding in a lake, Glacier National Park. No antlers, long pale legs, brown body.
author: naturenps
cardBack: Cow moose. No antlers, long legs, big nose, often with a calf. Look for the pale patch under the tail.

caption: Cow moose, head close up. Long drooping nose, big ears, a bell (flap of skin) under the throat.
author: Veronika Ronkos

caption: Shiras moose cow and calf, Wyoming. Never shoot a cow with a calf at side unless the rules say you may.
author: USFWS Mountain-Prairie

caption: Moose calf in spring, Alaska, beside its mother. Red brown and gangly; it stays with the cow its first year.
author: USFWSAlaska

caption: Moose calf in its first winter, Grand Teton. Smaller body, short face and no antlers: do not mistake it for a cow.
author: GrandTetonNPS

caption: Bull elk near Maligne Canyon, Jasper, Alberta. Dark mane, pale body, long swept back antlers with many tines.
author: Wilson Hui from Calgary, Canada
cardBack: Bull elk. Tan body, dark brown neck and mane, straw coloured rump, long antlers swept back over the body.

caption: Bull elk looking back. Note the straw coloured rump patch and the dark neck.
author: NPS Photo

caption: Bull elk at distance in snow, National Elk Refuge, Wyoming. Pale bodies and dark necks stand out a long way off.
author: USFWS Mountain Prairie

caption: Cow elk, Glacier National Park. No antlers, long neck, darker head and neck than the body.
author: GlacierNPS
cardBack: Cow elk. No antlers, tan body, dark head and neck, pale rump. Much bigger than a deer, smaller than a moose.

caption: Cow elk from behind, Firehole River, Yellowstone. The big pale rump patch is the elk signature.
author: Yellowstone National Park

caption: Cow elk herd in winter, Yellowstone. Elk live in herds; check every animal before you pick one.
author: Yellowstone National Park from Yellowstone NP, USA

caption: Black bear male, side view, near Whistler, BC. Back line highest at the rump, no shoulder hump, tall pointed ears.
author: Charles J. Sharp
cardBack: Black bear. No shoulder hump, straight face profile, tall ears, short curved claws. Colour does NOT tell you the species.

caption: Black bear face, Jasper. Straight profile from forehead to nose, tall ears, brown muzzle.
author: Thomas Fuhrmann

caption: Vancouver Island black bear on the shore at low tide, Tofino, BC. Coastal bears turn rocks for crabs.
author: Charles J. Sharp

caption: Brown phase black bear, Tatshenshini Alsek park, Yukon. Brown, but no hump and a straight face: still a black bear.
author: Diego Delso

caption: Cinnamon phase black bear eating dandelions, Waterton Lakes, Alberta. Light brown coat, tall ears, no hump.
author: Traveler100

caption: Pale brown black bear along the Dempster Highway, Yukon. Even this light coat sits on a black bear body shape.
author: Naturedata

caption: Black bear sow with two cubs, one black and one cinnamon, Yellowstone. Colour phases mix in one family. Cubs and sows with cubs are protected in BC (VERIFY page).
author: Neal Herbert

caption: Grizzly bear in sagebrush, Yellowstone. Big shoulder hump, dished face, short round ears.
author: NPS/Jim Peaco
cardBack: Grizzly bear. Shoulder hump, dished (concave) face, short round ears, long pale claws. Often silver tipped fur.

caption: Grizzly walking in snow, Yellowstone. The hump is the highest point of the back; the rump sits lower.
author: NPS/Jim Peaco

caption: Grizzly on a gravel bar, Noatak River, Alaska. From side on at distance, the hump shows clearly.
author: NPS Photo

caption: Grizzly face close up, Yellowstone. Dish between eyes and nose, small round ears, grizzled silver tips.
author: Terry Tollefsbol, NATIONAL CONSERVATION TRAINING CENTER-PUBLICATIONS AND TRAINING MATERIALS

caption: Grizzly sow with a yearling cub, Yellowstone. Never get between a sow and her cub.
author: NPS/Jim Peaco

caption: Mule deer running away, California. From behind: white rump, thin tail with a black tip, held down even when running.
author: Wingchi Poon

caption: Bighorn ram (left) and ewe, Wyoming. Ram: massive curled horns. Ewe: short, thin, slightly curved horns, like a goat's.
author: Bureau of Land Management

caption: Mule deer buck, side view, in snow, Siskiyou County, California. Grey coat, white rump, black tipped tail, forked antlers.
author: Marshal Hedin from San Diego
cardBack: Mule deer buck. Grey brown, white rump patch, thin white tail with a black tip, antlers that fork.

caption: Mule deer buck from behind, Colorado. Big white rump patch and a thin rope tail with a black tip.
author: USFWS Mountain-Prairie

caption: Mule deer buck in snow, Oregon. Practise counting the tips on each antler; forks on forks are the mule deer pattern.
author: Oregon Department of Fish & Wildlife

caption: Mule deer buck crossing open flats, Yellowstone. At 300 m you see a grey body, a white rump and antlers above the ears.
author: Yellowstone National Park

caption: Mule deer doe bounding across a road, Utah. A spooked mule deer often stots: all four feet push off together in a stiff legged bounce.
author: BLMUtah

caption: Young mule deer buck, Yellowstone. Count each antler: well under 4 tines a side. Not a 4 point buck.
author: Yellowstone National Park from Yellowstone NP, USA

caption: Young mule deer buck in velvet, Yosemite. Each antler is a simple fork: 2 points a side.
author: Guywelch2000

caption: Columbian black tailed deer buck in velvet, Mount Rainier, Washington. Smaller and darker than a mule deer; antlers still fork.
author: Charles J. Sharp

caption: Young black tailed buck, Victoria, BC. Note the wide tail, dark brown to black on top, held down.
author: Gordon Leggett

caption: Black tailed doe, Washington. The whole top of the tail is dark, not just the tip like a mule deer.
author: Walter Siegmund (talk)
cardBack: Black tailed deer. Coast deer. Tail wider than a mule deer's and dark or black all the way down the top.

caption: Young black tailed buck bedded by a highway, Ucluelet, Vancouver Island. Bedded deer show only head, ears and back.
author: Buiobuione

caption: Columbian black tailed buck in the Dungeness River, Washington, a doe at left. Red brown coat, dark tail, forked antlers like a mule deer.
author: Philip Cohen
cardBack: Black tailed buck. Forked antlers like a mule deer, but a smaller, darker deer with a wide tail dark all down the top.

caption: Three young mule deer bucks with small antlers, Wind Cave, South Dakota. Young bucks travel together; count every one.
author: NPS photo

caption: American wigeon drake, Reifel sanctuary, Ladner, BC. White crown stripe, green swoosh behind the eye, pinkish brown sides.
author: Judy Gallagher
cardBack: American wigeon drake. White forehead and crown (the baldpate), green band behind the eye, pink brown sides, small blue grey bill.

caption: American wigeon hen. Grey speckled head, warm orange brown sides, small blue grey bill with a black tip.
author: Mdf
cardBack: American wigeon hen. Plain grey head, rusty orange sides, short blue grey bill with a black tip.

caption: Green winged teal drake. Chestnut head with a green eye patch, a white bar down the side of the chest, cream patch under the tail.
author: Rhododendrites
cardBack: Green winged teal drake. Tiny duck, chestnut head with a green swoosh, white vertical bar in front of the wing.

caption: Green winged teal hen, California. Small brown duck, small dark bill, a flash of green in the wing.
author: Mike's Birds from Riverside, CA, US
cardBack: Green winged teal hen. Very small brown duck, small dark bill, green wing patch.

caption: Blue winged teal drake in flight, California. White crescent on the face, big pale blue patch on the front of the wing.
author: Frank Schulenburg

caption: Blue winged teal hen. Small brown duck with a dark eye line and a pale spot at the base of the bill.
author: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service - Midwest Region

caption: Gadwall drake. Plain grey body, black rear end, dark bill. The quiet grey duck.
author: Department of the Interior. U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service. National Conservation Training Center. 10/1997-8888
cardBack: Gadwall drake. Grey all over, black stern (rear end), dark bill, white patch in the wing.

caption: Gadwall drake in flight, Oregon. Look for the small square white patch on the back edge of the wing.
author: Oregon Department of Fish & Wildlife

caption: Gadwall hen, North Dakota. Like a mallard hen but slimmer, with an orange bill edged in dark and a white wing patch.
author: USFWS Mountain Prairie
cardBack: Gadwall hen. Mottled brown, orange sided bill with a dark top, white square in the wing (a mallard hen shows blue).

caption: Northern shoveler drake, North Dakota. Huge spoon bill, green head, white chest, chestnut sides.
author: USFWS Mountain Prairie
cardBack: Northern shoveler drake. Big spoon shaped bill, green head, white chest, rusty sides.

caption: Northern shoveler hen. Mottled brown, but the long spoon bill gives her away.
author: Charles J. Sharp
cardBack: Northern shoveler hen. Brown like a mallard hen, but with a long, wide spoon bill.

caption: Wood duck drake. Green crested head with white stripes, red eye, chestnut chest.
author: Rhododendrites
cardBack: Wood duck drake. Swept back green crest, white chin straps, red eye and bill base.

caption: Wood duck hen. Grey brown with a white teardrop around the eye and a small crest.
author: Russ
cardBack: Wood duck hen. Grey brown, white teardrop eye ring, small crest.

caption: Common goldeneye drake. Round white spot in front of the yellow eye, mostly white sides.
author: CheepShot
cardBack: Common goldeneye drake. Green black head, round white cheek spot, yellow eye, white sides.

caption: Common goldeneye hen. Chocolate brown head, yellow eye, grey body, dark bill with a yellow tip.
author: Charles J. Sharp

caption: Barrow's goldeneye drake, Wyoming. Crescent shaped white face patch, purple sheen on the head, a row of white spots on black sides.
author: USFWS Mountain-Prairie
cardBack: Barrow's goldeneye drake. White crescent (not a round spot) in front of the eye, more black on the back and sides.

caption: Barrow's goldeneye hen. Brown head, yellow eye, mostly yellow orange bill.
author: Pacific Southwest Region USFWS from Sacramento, US

caption: Bufflehead drake, California. Small black and white duck with a big white patch on the back of the head.
author: Mike's Birds from Riverside, CA, US
cardBack: Bufflehead drake. Tiny, mostly white, with a large white wedge on the back of a dark head.

caption: Bufflehead hen. Small grey brown duck with an oval white cheek patch.
author: Mdf
cardBack: Bufflehead hen. Very small, dark head, one white oval patch on the cheek.

caption: Ring necked duck drake, New Mexico. Peaked black head, white ring near the bill tip, white spur in front of the wing.
author: Chuck Homler d/b/a Focus On Wildlife
cardBack: Ring necked duck drake. Black back, grey sides with a white spur at the front, white ring around the bill.

caption: Ring necked duck hen. Brown, peaked head, white eye ring and a pale band on the bill.
author: Polinova

caption: Lesser scaup drake. Dark head, yellow eye, grey back, black chest and tail, white sides.
author: Chuck Homler d/b/a Focus On Wildlife
cardBack: Scaup drake. Black at both ends, white sides, grey back, yellow eye, blue bill.

caption: Lesser scaup hen. Brown with a white patch at the base of the bill.
author: Chuck Homler d/b/a Focus On Wildlife
cardBack: Scaup hen. Brown diving duck with a bold white patch around the bill base.

caption: Canvasback drake, Maryland. Long sloping forehead into a black bill, rusty head, white body.
author: Judy Gallagher
cardBack: Canvasback drake. Red brown head, long sloping black bill and forehead, bright white back.

caption: Canvasback hen. Pale brown head and grey body, same long sloping profile as the drake.
author: Judy Gallagher

caption: Redhead drake. Round red head, grey body, blue grey bill with a black tip.
author: Rhododendrites
cardBack: Redhead drake. Round red head, grey back, blue bill with a white ring and black tip.

caption: Redhead hen, Ontario. Plain brown with a rounded head and a blue grey bill.
author: Mykola Swarnyk

caption: Common merganser drake, Toronto. Long thin red bill, dark green head, white body. A fish eating duck.
author: Mykola Swarnyk

caption: Common merganser hen. Shaggy rusty head, thin red bill, clean white chin.
author: USFWSmidwest

caption: Hooded merganser drake. White fan shaped crest edged in black, thin dark bill.
author: Peterwchen

caption: Hooded merganser hen. Cinnamon bushy crest, thin bill.
author: Peterwchen

caption: Diving ducks running across the water to take off, South Dakota. Divers patter along the surface; puddle ducks jump straight up.
author: USFWS Mountain Prairie

caption: Ducks flushing off a wetland, Nebraska. Pick one bird before you shoot, and know what it is.
author: USFWS Mountain Prairie

caption: Mallards taking off over a lake. Drakes show green heads; every bird shows the blue wing patch.
author: Jocelyn Anderson

caption: Northern pintail hen in flight. Long neck, slim body, pointed tail, plain brown head.
author: Frank Schulenburg

caption: Canada goose. Black neck and head, white chin strap, brown body. Large, with a long neck.
author: Joe Ravi
cardBack: Canada goose. Black head and neck, white chin strap, brown grey body, long neck.

caption: Cackling goose. Same pattern as a Canada goose but mallard sized, with a short neck and a stubby bill.
author: VJAnderson
cardBack: Cackling goose. Looks like a small Canada goose: short neck, tiny stubby bill, square head.

caption: Cackling geese with a Canada goose (right). Compare size, neck length and bill length.
author: Andy Reago & Chrissy McClarren

caption: Snow goose. White body, black wing tips, pink bill with a black grin patch.
author: Paul Danese
cardBack: Snow goose. White with black wing tips; pink bill with a dark grin patch.

caption: Ross's goose. A small white goose with a stubby bill and no black grin patch.
author: Andrew C

caption: Snow goose (left) and Ross's goose (right). The Ross's is smaller, with a short bill and a round head.
author: Nomdeploom

caption: Greater white fronted goose in flight. Grey brown, white band at the bill base, black bars on the belly.
author: Frank Schulenburg

caption: Black brant, San Diego. Small dark goose, black neck with a white necklace. A coastal goose.
author: Lucwrte
